valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 16 Nov 2026. (1) Business: an insurance broker (InsureMe, 84% of FY2026 revenue and nearly all profit) earning commissions from insurers, plus DIGIS, an insurtech software house (16% of revenue, about break-even). A broker takes no underwriting risk, so it is valued as a service business, not an insurer. Weighted by revenue, since DIGIS's profit is near zero and profit weights would ignore it: 80% broking, 20% software. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. Stand-ins: Insurance (General), global, January 2026, unlevered beta 0.42, cash-corrected 0.47 (web-search extract of his global table); Software (Internet) global unlevered, cash-corrected 1.34 (as used for PKME.N0000, 15 Nov 2026). 0.8 × 0.47 + 0.2 × 1.34 = 0.64. (3) Net cash (Rs 135.5mn at Sep 2026, leases included), so debt to equity 0 and no relevering: 0.64. (4) Local 5-year betas: none exist. The share listed in December 2025 and only 1.27% is in public hands (26,179 shares), so it trades thinly and any local beta would be ignored anyway. (5) Higher of 0.64 and (no local figure) = 0.64. (6) Within 0.3–2, but low for a tiny, illiquid company: the insurance figure reflects big diversified insurers, so the bear case's +1.5 points on the cost of equity matters here. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (16 Nov 2026): net cash Rs 135.5mn at Sep 2026 against a market cap of about Rs 3.6bn at Rs 1,749.75, so debt weight 0% and WACC equals the cost of equity. Cost of debt 6.79% is lease interest for part of 2025/26.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 10% / 18% / 25%; supported about 26% on underlying figures (reinvestment 62% of after-tax operating profit × return on capital about 42%). All within it.
valuationInputs.reason: The calculator prints 244% (reinvestment rate 105% × return on capital 232%) because 2025/26 operating profit includes the Rs 56.6mn one-off, working capital includes its non-cash reversal, and opening capital at March 2025 was only about Rs 32mn. Underlying: capex 26.3 − depreciation 11.4 + working capital 7.5 = 22.4 on after-tax underlying operating profit 35.9 (62%); trailing after-tax operating profit 48.4 on Sep 2026 capital 115.7 (equity 251.3 − net cash 135.5) = 42%.

valuationInputs.name: Growth
valuationInputs.value: Bear 10% then 5% / Base 18% then 6% / Bull 25% then 7%
valuationInputs.reason: Five years, then long-run below the 12.24% bond and WACC; long-run reinvestment = growth ÷ return on new capital. Revenue grew 40% in 2025/26 and 38% in H1 2026/27.

valuationInputs.reason: No company split. Bear = average capex booked over two years; bull = depreciation and amortisation (incl. right-of-use); base = middle. Most capex is DIGIS software development (growth).

valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS Rs 14.79; H2 Rs 10.00 / 14.00 / 17.00 (underlying H2 last year about Rs 11.92). Justified forward P/E, two-stage. Base 37% below the Rs 45.98 trailing run-rate, which includes the one-off of Rs 19.27 a share; 8% above the underlying Rs 26.71.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Underlying ROE 21.5% (2025/26), about 27% trailing; faded over ten years in residual income.

valuationInputs.name: R&D
valuationInputs.reason: Software development is capitalised under LKAS 38 (Rs 19.6mn and Rs 21.8mn, about 4–5% of revenue) and already counted as capex; expensed R&D isn't disclosed, and only two years of figures exist, under the three the rule needs.

changeLog.basedOn: Annual Report 2025/26 and interim to 30 Sep 2026 (CSE downloads)
changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/add INME.N0000). First analysis. Research record built from the two downloaded reports (FY 2025 and FY 2026 annual figures, reinvestment figures, Q1, Q2 and H1 FY2027). The 2025/26 profit includes a one-off Rs 56.6mn reversal of Dialog revenue share; all methods use underlying earnings. Beta 0.64 (provisional; Damodaran stand-ins from web search, no local 5-year beta) gives cost of equity and WACC 14.8%. Methods: DCF 384, P/E 338, justified P/B 263, residual income 308 (weighted). Business tests 2 of 4 (fails returns, not proven over several years, and steady profit): category 3, avoid for now. Price is the last trade at 30 Sep 2026 from the interim report (CSE site not reachable from this run). The calculator's growth check (244%) is distorted by the one-off; the underlying figure (about 26%) is used. Earlier years' figures weren't available.
